questions.stem: Which feature made smallpox a good candidate for eradication?

options.B: An animal reservoir allowed targeted culling
options.E: Patients were most contagious before symptoms appeared

questions.explanation: Smallpox features: direct person-to-person spread with no vector or reservoir, a distinctive rash that made diagnosis easy, lifelong immunity in survivors, and severe symptoms that kept infectious patients in bed. B, C: There was no reservoir or vector. D: The distinctive rash made cases obvious. E: Once infectious, patients were bedridden and infected few others.

questions.stem: USAID funding a vaccination program in one partner country is an example of which kind of global-health player?
questions.explanation: Bilateral organizations involve one donor and one recipient. A: Banks are owned by many member states. B: UN agencies are multilateral. C: Movements are networks of activists. D: USAID is governmental.

questions.stem: Which global-health challenge does the lecture link specifically to large private foundations such as the Gates Foundation?
questions.explanation: The growing influence of philanthropic organizations in setting priorities raises questions about accountability, transparency and priority-setting. A: Linked to multiple institutions, donors and actors. B: Linked to WHO's limited, unevenly distributed funding. D: Infectious disease, NCDs, emergencies and climate change at once. E: Linked to differences in national resources.

questions.stem: Which risk factor is linked to the top ten causes of death worldwide?
questions.explanation: Tobacco is related to all top ten causes of mortality. A: Linked mainly to HIV and STIs. B: Linked to diarrheal disease. C: Linked to infection susceptibility. E: Not listed.

questions.stem: Which global-health player is owned and governed by member states and provides long-term loans and grants to low- and middle-income countries?

options.C: Multilateral development bank such as the World Bank

questions.explanation: Multilateral development banks (World Bank, African, Asian and Inter-American Development Banks) are owned by member states and mobilize development financing through loans, grants and technical assistance. A: WHO gives technical assistance, standards and coordination. B: One donor country, one recipient. D: Fosters public-health collaboration among member states. E: Loose activist networks that shape the agenda.

questions.stem: Although a smallpox vaccine existed since 1796, what made eradication a practical goal in the 1950s?

options.B: The vaccine could be mass-produced and stored without refrigeration
options.C: Creation of the WHO Smallpox Eradication Unit
options.D: Mandatory case reporting by all WHO member states
options.E: Discovery that smallpox had no animal reservoir

questions.explanation: Eradication became practical once the vaccine could be mass-produced and stored without refrigeration. A: The bifurcated needle (1960s) was a later breakthrough that cut costs. C, D: Parts of the later WHO campaign, not what made the goal practical. E: A disease feature that made smallpox a good candidate, not the 1950s development.
